bug_description.normalized: When the attacker-controlled font is shaped against the harness's fixed UTF-8 string, HarfBuzz's AAT `morx` chain first reaches an attacker-controlled end-of-text `InsertionSubtable` entry. In the vulnerable current-insert path, `transition` checks only `!before`, so with `buffer->idx == buffer->len` it still calls `buffer->copy_glyph()` and `buffer->skip_glyph()`, copying `info[len]` from spare heap capacity left uninitialized by `hb_buffer_t::enlarge`. The same entry also outputs at least one glyph, and for the later crash to occur in a separate `NoncontextualSubtable` it must take the `move_to(end + count)` arm, leaving the copied pseudo-glyph in `out_info` for `swap_buffers()` to publish. A later noncontextual `morx` subtable then iterates that pseudo-glyph and passes its uninitialized `codepoint` into `LookupFormat0::get_value`, where MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value at `glyph_id >= num_glyphs`. The staged `patch.diff` / `fixed_commit` only modify `src/hb-aat-layout-kerx-table.hh`, so they do not resolve this witnessed `morx` insertion bug.

source.code: unsigned int klass = buffer->idx < buffer->len ? machine.get_class (info[buffer->idx].codepoint, num_glyphs) : (unsigned) StateTable<EntryData>::CLASS_END_OF_TEXT; const Entry<EntryData> *entry = machine.get_entryZ (state, klass);
source.description: First project statement on the witnessed vulnerable path that materializes attacker-controlled `morx` state. On the crashing iteration `buffer->idx == buffer->len`, so the driver selects `CLASS_END_OF_TEXT` and fetches the corresponding insertion entry whose flags and indices drive the copy-after-current path.
source.value_from: The PoC font's AAT `morx` insertion state table supplies the `entryTable` data fetched here while the harness shapes the fixed UTF-8 string `ABCDEXYZ123@_%&)*$!`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. The later noncontextual lookup reuses the copied pseudo-glyph's uninitialized `codepoint` as `glyph_id`, and this bounds comparison is the first executed use of that indeterminate value on the saved path.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The current-insert path treats `!before` as sufficient to copy a current glyph, but on the end-of-text entry there is no live current glyph. The vulnerable code omits the required `buffer->idx < buffer->len` guard before `copy_glyph()` and the matching `skip_glyph()` call, so it copies `info[len]` from uninitialized tail storage.

parser_admitted.description: The witness font's `morx` chain contains an `Insertion` subtable, so dispatch enters `InsertionSubtable::apply` on attacker-controlled table data before the later crashing noncontextual subtable runs.
parser_admitted.condition: The selected `morx` chain subtable type equals `AAT::ChainSubtable::Insertion` (5), making the vulnerable insertion state-machine path reachable.

published_to_next_subtable.description: For the copied pseudo-glyph to be consumed by a later `NoncontextualSubtable` rather than by the insertion driver itself, the selected current-insert entry must output at least one glyph and take the `end + count` arm here. That combination leaves the copied slot in `out_info` so `swap_buffers()` publishes it to subsequent subtables.
published_to_next_subtable.condition: The saved crash occurs in a later `NoncontextualSubtable`, so on this path `count > 0` and `!(flags & DontAdvance)` are required for the copied pseudo-glyph to survive subtable termination.

tainted_value_origin.description: MSAN allocation origin. Growing the fixed-text glyph-info array creates spare heap slots that `realloc()` does not zero. Later `hb_buffer_t::add()` initializes only the live glyph range, leaving the first tail slot `info[len]` indeterminate when the end-of-text insertion bug copies it.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The harness's first `hb_buffer_add_utf8(buffer, text, -1, 0, -1)` call triggers `ensure()` and `enlarge()` before the crashing `hb_shape()` invocation.

fine_trace.note: MSAN allocation origin. The fixed-text buffer grows its `info` array via `realloc()`, which leaves the newly added tail slots uninitialized.

fine_trace.code: memset (glyph, 0, sizeof (*glyph)); glyph->codepoint = codepoint; glyph->mask = 0; glyph->cluster = cluster;
fine_trace.note: Appending the harness's fixed UTF-8 string initializes only the live slot at each current `info[len]`. After the final glyph is added, the next tail slot `info[len]` still contains whatever step 1's allocation left behind.

fine_trace.code: unsigned int klass = buffer->idx < buffer->len ? machine.get_class (info[buffer->idx].codepoint, num_glyphs) : (unsigned) StateTable<EntryData>::CLASS_END_OF_TEXT; const Entry<EntryData> *entry = machine.get_entryZ (state, klass);
fine_trace.note: Source step. On the vulnerability-causing iteration `buffer->idx == buffer->len`, so the insertion driver selects `CLASS_END_OF_TEXT` and fetches the corresponding attacker-controlled entry from the PoC font's `morx` state table.

fine_trace.code: if (entry->data.currentInsertIndex != 0xFFFF) { unsigned int count = (flags & CurrentInsertCount) >> 5; unsigned int start = entry->data.currentInsertIndex; const GlyphID *glyphs = &insertionAction[start]; if (unlikely (!c->sanitizer.check_array (glyphs, count))) return false; }
fine_trace.note: The selected end-of-text entry enables current insertion and materializes its insertion list. The saved MSAN store-origin stack also includes `hb_buffer_t::output_glyph()` from line 651, so this witnessed path has `count > 0` and appends at least one glyph after the copied slot.

The same entry's flag word clears `CurrentInsertBefore`, so `before` is false and the current-insert path will try to copy and then skip a current glyph even though the driver is already at end-of-text.

Root cause. This guard checks only `!before`, so on the end-of-text path it still copies a current glyph even though `buffer->idx == buffer->len` means no live current glyph exists. The missing predicate is `buffer->idx < buffer->len`.

With `idx == len`, `copy_glyph()` reads the first unused glyph-info slot `info[len]` and copies that entire uninitialized record into the out-of-place output buffer. The copied pseudo-glyph therefore carries an uninitialized `codepoint`.

The insertion loop appends the entry's inserted glyphs after the copied slot. At this point `out_info[end]` is the copied pseudo-glyph from step 7 and `out_info[end + 1 .. end + count]` are the newly inserted glyphs.
Because `before` is false, the code also skips the nonexistent current glyph. Starting from end-of-text, this advances `idx` from `len` to `len + 1` before the subsequent rewind decision.

For the saved crash to happen in a later `NoncontextualSubtable`, this call must take the `end + count` arm. Because step 4 established `count > 0`, rewinding to `end + count` removes only the last inserted glyph, leaving the copied pseudo-glyph from step 7 in `out_info[end]` so it survives subtable termination.

fine_trace.code: if (out_info != info) { info = out_info; out_info = tmp_string; pos = (hb_glyph_position_t *) out_info; } ... len = out_len; ... idx = 0;
fine_trace.note: Insertion runs out-of-place, so when the driver finishes `swap_buffers()` publishes the surviving `out_info` span as the active `buffer->info` array. The copied pseudo-glyph left at `out_info[end]` by step 10 is now inside the live `info[0 .. len - 1]` range for subsequent subtables.

fine_trace.code: for (unsigned int i = 0; i < count; i++) { const GlyphID *replacement = substitute.get_value (info[i].codepoint, num_glyphs); }
fine_trace.note: A later noncontextual `morx` subtable iterates the published glyph buffer. When `i` reaches the copied pseudo-glyph from step 11, its uninitialized `codepoint` is forwarded unchanged into `substitute.get_value()` as the lookup key.

MSAN sink. `glyph_id` is the same scalar forwarded at step 12 from the copied pseudo-glyph's uninitialized `codepoint`, so this comparison is the first executed use of the indeterminate value on the saved crash path.

allocation_context.note: The MSAN origin reports a heap allocation at `realloc`; the first project frame in that origin chain is `hb_buffer_t::enlarge`, reached from `hb_buffer_add_utf<hb_utf8_t>` while the harness loads the fixed UTF-8 string.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Partial — the allocation context explains why `info[len]` is uninitialized, but the bug is the later end-of-text current-insert `copy_glyph()` plus publication of that copied slot to a later noncontextual subtable.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` / `fixed_commit` only modify `src/hb-aat-layout-kerx-table.hh` to use `sanitizer.get_num_glyphs()`. The witnessed uninitialized-value chain is created in `src/hb-aat-layout-morx-table.hh`, `src/hb-buffer.hh`, and `src/hb-buffer.cc`, so the provided patch does not address the saved crash path.

format.name: sfnt font with AAT morx chain
format.contract: A font blob accepted by `hb_face_create()` and exercised through the harness's first UTF-8 `hb_shape(font, buffer, NULL, 0)` call on `ABCDEXYZ123@_%&)*$!`. On the saved crash path, the font's `morx` chain reaches an end-of-text `InsertionSubtable` entry whose current-insert arm is active, clears `CurrentInsertBefore`, and outputs at least one glyph; the later noncontextual crash further requires that entry to clear `DontAdvance` so `move_to(end + count)` leaves the copied pseudo-glyph in `out_info` for `swap_buffers()`. A following `NoncontextualSubtable` then consumes that published pseudo-glyph's uninitialized `codepoint` in `LookupFormat0::get_value`. The staged evidence does not justify a broader trigger class than fonts reproducing this witnessed insertion-then-noncontextual chain.
